findings.change: Optional: give the publisher an injected stderr writer so the test can stay in-process. No change is required for this unit.
findings.claim: The commit adds a fourth test that the brief does not name, TestProgressWriteFailuresRecoverAndReportOnce. To capture what the publisher prints on stderr, it starts the test binary again as a child process. It tests a real clause of the contract: a failed write is reported once until a write succeeds. It does not depend on wall time. It is still a real-process test where an injected stderr writer would have been enough.
findings.evidence: runner_progress_test.go:234-260 runs exec.Command(os.Args[0], "-test.run=...") and expects exactly two 'publish steward runner progress:' lines. The test passed under the race detector. It does not wait on time or observe process state, so R-104-m1e (the artificial-clock ruling) does not apply. Not material: the change works and is safe without any edit.

findings.change: None required. Later units should pass 0 for arbitration waits, as the brief already says.
findings.claim: Wait ignores a positive duration unless the reason is 'idle' or 'external'. A call like Wait("arbitration", d) therefore silently records no deadline. This matches the brief: a deadline exists only for 'idle' and for an 'external' wait whose owner has one. But a later unit (U1b to U1d) that passes the wrong reason with a duration would lose the deadline without any warning.
findings.evidence: runner_progress.go Wait: `if within > 0 && (reason == "idle" || reason == "external")`. No caller in U1a passes arbitration with a duration. Not material: U1a works and is safe as it stands.
